'''Michael Darwin Morley''' (September 29, 1930 – October 11, 2020) was an American [[mathematician]].  At his death in 2020, Morley was professor emeritus at [[Cornell University]]. His research was in [[mathematical logic]] and [[model theory]], and he is best known for [[Morley's categoricity theorem]], which he proved in his PhD thesis ''Categoricity in Power'' in 1962.

==Early life and education==
Morley was born in [[Youngstown, Ohio]], on September 29, 1930.<ref name=cornell>{{cite web|url=https://math.cornell.edu/michael-morley-professor-emeritus-mathematics-dies-90|title=Michael Morley, Professor Emeritus of Mathematics, dies at 90|website=Department of Mathematics, Cornell University|access-date=14 October 2020|archive-date=14 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201014202606/https://math.cornell.edu/michael-morley-professor-emeritus-mathematics-dies-90|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=AMSnotices>{{cite journal|author=<!-- no author given --> |volume=50 |issue=4 |pages=462–467 |title=2003 Steele Prizes|date=April 2003 |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200304/comm-steele.pdf| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807094731/https://www.ams.org/notices/200304/comm-steele.pdf |archive-date=August 7, 2020 |url-status=live |access-date=October 17, 2020}}</ref> He obtained his BS in mathematics from [[Case Institute of Technology]] in 1951 and his PhD in mathematics from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1962. Morley's formal PhD advisor at the University of Chicago was [[Saunders Mac Lane]], but he completed his thesis under the guidance of [[Robert Vaught]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name=cornell/> His dissertation was titled ''Categoricity in Power''.<ref name=MGP>{{MathGenealogy|id=6512|title=Michael Darwin Morley}}</ref>

==Career==
Morley was an assistant professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] from 1963 to 1967. He joined the faculty at [[Cornell University]] in 1967 as an associate professor, was promoted to professor in 1970, and became a professor emeritus in 2003.<ref name=cornell/> He served as president of the [[Association for Symbolic Logic]] from 1986 to 1989.<ref name=cornell/>

Morley received the 2003 [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Seminal Contribution to Research from the [[American Mathematical Society]] for his 1965 paper "Categoricity in Power". This paper, his doctoral dissertation, introduced [[Morley rank]] and proved [[Morley's categoricity theorem]].<ref name=cornell/><ref name=AMSnotices/> 

==Personal life==
Morley died on October 11, 2020, in [[Sayre, Pennsylvania]].<ref name=cornell/>
